description:
Split out of op-wpi0 / gh:#43, where it was the blocking child op-q2ec. Filed separately because it is NOT one crate's problem — it lands in raffles and tampines for different reasons and neither use is a subset of the other. gh:#44 https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/44

CURRENT STATE, surveyed 2026-09-04. raffles/src/surrogate.rs is 54 lines with NO pub items — a stub. sensitivity.rs is real (Sobol sample layout, Pearson and Spearman correlation, input-output correlations) but that is sampling and sensitivity, not a surrogate: no Gaussian process, no polynomial chaos, no POD, no response surface of any kind. tampines has nothing either — one incidental interpolation in multiphase_1d/drift_flux.rs and no tabulation or reduced-order layer anywhere.

WHY IT MATTERS IN RAFFLES. raffles is a pure-Rust port of RAVEN's UQ and risk core, and ROM is RAVEN's OWN first-class concept — upstream ships GP, polynomial chaos, SVM and more under exactly that name. This is not a new idea bolted on; it is a port that stops short of one of upstream's defining capabilities. The sampling half already being present makes the omission more conspicuous: raffles can design an experiment and analyse its outputs, but cannot build a model from them.

OWNERSHIP — READ BEFORE ACTING. raffles has a named owner, Adolphus Lye, and the crate's own docs state it is theirs to steer and that changes of direction are their call. Adding a ROM layer is a DIRECTION CALL, not a defect fix. This bead proposes it; it does not authorise it. Route to the owner before any implementation.

WHY IT MATTERS IN TAMPINES. Different reason entirely. tampines holds the expensive, repeatedly evaluated physics — steam and gas properties, HEM critical flow, drift flux, packed-bed conjugate heat transfer, KTA and ZBS closures. Those are the inner loop of every transient, and a twin at interactive rates cannot afford a full property or closure evaluation per tick per node. The standard answer is tabulation or a fitted surrogate over the state space and tampines has neither. Same constraint driving op-1z3o.13 (real-time pacing).

THE TWO NEEDS ARE DISTINCT. raffles = the ROM FRAMEWORK (fit/evaluate/validate over sampled data), driven by RAVEN fidelity, general over arbitrary inputs, owner's call. tampines = a CONSUMER plus a specific use (fast property/closure evaluation), driven by real-time twin operation, tabulated or fitted forms of known correlations, ordinary engineering. tampines should consume what raffles provides rather than growing a parallel surrogate — but if the raffles direction call goes the other way, tampines still needs its tabulation layer and that path must not be blocked on it.

WHY THE PIPELINE FORCED IT. op-wpi0's chain is ENDF -> MC -> MGXS+feedback -> deterministic -> ROM -> digital twin. Stage 5 is this. Either it gets built or the chain becomes deterministic -> twin directly and all seven reactor children simplify. The decision comes BEFORE any reactor child starts because it changes all of them.

WHAT DECIDES IT is measurable, not a matter of taste: run the deterministic solve (genfoam / bedok / moltres) for a representative transient, time it, compare against the twin's tick budget. Clears it -> drop stage 5 and say so. Does not -> the surrogate is load-bearing and its absence is why the twin cannot run.

NATURAL COMPOSITION. op-84bc / gh:#42 will already produce cross sections over a state grid of temperature, density and burnup, because genfoam::xs::NuclearDataOneEnergy takes parametrised cross sections. That is the same shape a surrogate wants — sampled inputs, expensive outputs, fit a model. Doing either without knowing about the other wastes the overlap.

NOT IN SCOPE: choosing the surrogate family. GP vs polynomial chaos vs POD follows from the measurement above rather than preceding it.

Related: op-wpi0 / gh:#43, op-84bc / gh:#42, op-1z3o.13.
title: Reduced-order models / surrogates: absent in raffles, needed in tampines

description: Structural gap found during the op-sr4n survey: bibliography.rs's BibliographyState.root is a raw String feeding crate::project::regenerate (the OLDER pdf/+markdown/+line-range kovan.toml format, root.rs's own doc comment distinguishes it from the new KovanRoot/entity.rs format). It cannot 'jump to citekey X' against a KovanRoot today. mindmap.rs's bib_display (reads root.bibliography_path() + kovan_literature::parse_bib_entries) is the working precedent to follow. Out of scope for the first activate_paper pass (op-sr4n.1-5); do not block those on this.
title: activate_paper: 6 (deferred): migrate bibliography.rs off the old project.rs format onto KovanRoot

description:
Give OPCPFluidArray (rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs) a subset of tuas_boussinesq_solver's
FluidArray interface, so a future TAMPINES Pipe component can enum-dispatch
between a TUAS backend and a coolprop backend interchangeably. Scope
(confirmed with user via plan-mode session 2026-07-13, see
outram-park-dt-plan.md at workspace root and the full planning-tool record):

- New fields: lateral_adjacent_array_temperature_vector/conductance_vector
  (Vec<Vec<T>>, not Array1 -- coolprop has no ndarray dep), q_vector/
  q_fraction_vector (heat source), wetted_perimeter, incline_angle,
  mass_flowrate, pressure_loss, internal_pressure_source.
- Simplified vs TUAS: no NusseltCorrelation or DimensionlessDarcyLossCorrelations
  port -- caller supplies conductance/pressure-loss values directly.
- Lateral coupling + heat source wired into step()'s energy equation now
  (one-line addition to the existing explicit source-term loop, alongside
  conv_he/dp_dt). Geometry/flow-bookkeeping fields stay pure bookkeeping,
  not read by step() (matches TUAS itself).
- New error type OPCPFluidArrayError::LengthMismatch (own type, not a
  MeshError reuse), properly re-exported from lib.rs (fixes the existing
  MeshError-not-exported gap in the same pass).
- New file rhoPimpleFoam/lateral_coupling.rs (mirrors TUAS's own
  directory-per-concern split for this exact feature) -- 13 new methods,
  7 new tests.
- set_temperature_vector needs a real per-cell (p,T) flash + write
  he/rho/t/psi together, NOT a plain t field write (he is the actual PIMPLE
  state variable; a plain t write would be silently undone by the next
  correct_thermo() call).

This is Part 1 of a 3-part plan (Part 2: new tampines crate, Part 3: new
outram-park-digital-twin-gui crate) -- this bead covers Part 1 only.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: Done 2026-07-13: lateral_coupling.rs created (13 methods, 7 tests), new() field initializers added, step() wires lateral conductance + heat source into the energy-equation source term (extensive Watts, matching conv_he/dp_dt units), clear_vectors() called at end of step(). OPCPFluidArrayError re-exported from lib.rs. Test fix: test fluid changed from Water (liquid at 300K/1bar -- unreachable by the vapor-branch flash, silently no-ops every correct_thermo/state_pt call) to Nitrogen (matches existing passing tests' fluid choice). Also found t/rho lag he by one outer-corrector iteration in this PIMPLE solver -- tests call correct_thermo() after step() to sync t before reading temperature. Verified: cargo build --release clean, cargo test --release 248 lib tests passed (241 existing + 7 new) + all integration tests green, cargo check --workspace --lib --tests --release clean (no downstream breakage).

title: Extend OPCPFluidArray with TUAS-FluidArray-like interface (lateral coupling, heat source, geometry, flow bookkeeping)

description: Pitzer ion-interaction virial model for activity coefficients at high ionic strength (>0.5 m), beyond the Debye-Huckel/Davies range already in src/activity. Standalone module. Split from op-v6s.15.1.
title: Pitzer activity model (high-ionic-strength brines)
